entries.name: Build a sentence with a target word
entries.summary: Write one sentence that uses a given word
entries.trains: putting a word to use yourself
entries.doesNotDo: Each sentence stands on its own. Nothing in it exercises holding a thought across several sentences, which is where most learners actually break down — and the check finds spelling and agreement, not word order, word choice or idiom.

entries.name: Writing freely
entries.summary: Write freely on a prompt, with nothing to copy from
entries.trains: writing under your own steam — and what you steer around
entries.doesNotDo: It cannot make you use what you are dodging. Steering around a word is what it reveals, not what it repairs.

entries.name: Diary, three sentences
entries.doesNotDo: It circles the same life. Your days repeat, so the vocabulary it demands narrows rather than widens over months.

entries.name: Summarising what you read
entries.summary: Say what a text said, shorter, in writing
entries.doesNotDo: It lets you lift phrases straight out. Without a deliberate pause between reading and writing, much of what appears is copied rather than your own.

entries.name: Back-translation with comparison
entries.summary: Translate out, translate back, compare with the original
entries.trains: structure, and it makes avoidance visible
entries.doesNotDo: It grades you against one wording. A different wording that is perfectly good will show up as a mistake, and the comparison cannot tell the two apart.

entries.name: Copying out a good paragraph
entries.summary: Copy out a well-written paragraph by hand
entries.doesNotDo: It involves no choice at all. Every word is given, so it is handwriting and attention practice, not language production.

entries.name: Rewriting a text in your own words
entries.summary: Say the same thing again, differently
entries.doesNotDo: It rewards saying it another way over saying it precisely, and someone short of vocabulary will reformulate downwards into what they already have.

entries.name: Captioning your own photos
entries.summary: Write a line under a photo of your own
entries.trains: vocabulary you have a connection to
entries.doesNotDo: It cannot be aimed. What your photos happen to contain decides the vocabulary, and that is unlikely to be what you most need.

entries.name: Translating a song
entries.summary: Work out what a song you like actually says
entries.doesNotDo: Lyrics are unrepresentative. Inverted word order and archaic vocabulary are normal in songs and wrong in speech.

entries.name: Writing and performing a play
entries.summary: Write something short and put it on
entries.doesNotDo: It runs for weeks and produces one measurement. As a project it is excellent; as something to measure you by, nearly useless.
